DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS

You were admitted with new-onset atrial fibrillation. Rate control was achieved and anticoagulation has been initiated for stroke prophylaxis.

MEDICATIONS
- Warfarin 5 mg PO QHS. Your dose will be titrated according to INR.
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO BID.
- Pantoprazole 40 mg PO QD for gastric prophylaxis.

ANTICOAGULATION PRECAUTIONS
- Do not take aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen. These potentiate bleeding.
- Maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K containing foods. Do not abruptly increase or decrease leafy green vegetables.
- Abstain from alcohol.
- Use an electric razor and a soft toothbrush.

FOLLOW-UP
- The anticoagulation clinic will check your INR in 3 days.
- Follow up with cardiology in 2 weeks.
- Follow up with your primary care physician in 4 weeks.

SEEK IMMEDIATE MEDICAL ATTENTION FOR:
- Bleeding that will not stop after 10 minutes of pressure
- Blood in the urine or stool, or black tarry stool
- A severe headache, or any head injury however minor
- New weakness or numbness on one side
- Syncope

Call the anticoagulation clinic for any missed warfarin dose. Do not double a dose to compensate.

CARDIAC SURGERY DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS

Procedure: coronary artery bypass grafting x 3, with saphenous vein harvest from the left leg.

MEDICATIONS
- Aspirin 81 mg PO QD indefinitely. Do not stop this without speaking to your surgeon.
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO BID.
- Atorvastatin 80 mg PO QHS.
- Lisinopril 5 mg PO QD.
- Furosemide 20 mg PO QD for 7 days, then stop.
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq PO QD for 7 days.
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg PO q8h scheduled.
- Oxycodone 5 mg PO q6h PRN severe pain. Not more than 4 tablets in 24 hours.
- Docusate 100 mg PO BID.

STERNAL PRECAUTIONS - OBSERVE FOR 8 WEEKS
- No lifting, pushing, or pulling anything over 10 pounds.
- Do not push up from a chair with your arms. Use your legs.
- Do not reach behind your back or above your head.
- No driving for 6 weeks.

INCISION CARE
- Shower daily. Do not soak in a bath until cleared.
- Do not apply lotion or powder to the sternal incision or the leg incision.
- Wear the compression stocking on the harvest leg during the day. Remove at night.

ACTIVITY
- Walk daily, increasing by 5 minutes each day as tolerated.
- Elevate the harvest leg when seated.
- Cardiac rehabilitation begins in 4 weeks.

FOLLOW-UP
- Follow up with cardiac surgery in 2 weeks.
- Follow up with cardiology in 4 weeks.
- Follow up with your primary care physician in 3 weeks.

CALL THE CARDIAC SURGERY OFFICE IMMEDIATELY FOR:
- Temperature above 101 F
- Sternal instability, a clicking or shifting sensation in the breastbone
- Erythema, induration, or purulent drainage from either incision
- Weight gain over 3 pounds in one day
- Palpitations or an irregular heartbeat
- Increasing dyspnea or peripheral edema

CALL 911 FOR CHEST PAIN, SEVERE DYSPNEA, OR SYNCOPE.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT OBSERVATION DISCHARGE

Diagnosis: cellulitis of the right lower extremity.

You received intravenous cefazolin in the observation unit. The erythema has demarcated and you are suitable for oral therapy at home.

Take cephalexin 500 mg PO QID for 10 days. Complete the full course. Take acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain or fever.

Elevate the extremity above the level of your heart whenever you are seated or lying down. This is as important as the antibiotic.

The border of the erythema has been marked with a pen. Do not wash the mark off. It allows you and your doctor to see whether the infection is advancing.

Do not apply any topical antibiotic ointment. Do not soak the leg.

Follow up with your primary care physician in 2 days so the margin can be reassessed. A wound care referral has been placed if the skin breaks down.

Return to the emergency department immediately if the erythema advances beyond the marked border, if you develop fever above 101 F, if you see purulent drainage or a fluctuant area, if the pain becomes severe and out of proportion to the appearance, or if you notice crepitus or skin necrosis.

You were admitted for an exacerbation of congestive heart failure with volume overload. Diuresis was achieved with intravenous furosemide and you have been transitioned to an oral regimen.

- Weight gain of more than 3 pounds in one day
- Increasing dyspnea or orthopnea
- Edema of the lower extremities that is worsening
- Palpitations
- Syncope or near-syncope

Call 911 if you develop chest pain or severe shortness of breath at rest.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DISCHARGE: MILD TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY

Your CT of the head showed no acute intracranial abnormality. You have sustained a concussion.

MEDICATIONS
- Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN headache. Do not exceed 3000 mg in 24 hours.
- Ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN nausea.
- Do not take ibuprofen, naproxen, or aspirin for 72 hours. These increase the risk of intracranial bleeding.

COGNITIVE AND PHYSICAL REST
- Relative rest for 48 hours, then graded return to activity as symptoms permit.
- No screens for 24 hours, then limit screen exposure as tolerated.
- No return to sport, contact activity, or any activity with a fall risk until cleared by a physician. A second impact before recovery can be catastrophic.
- No driving until you are symptom free and off all sedating medication.
- Abstain from alcohol for 2 weeks.
- No strenuous exercise until cleared.

SLEEP
- You may sleep normally. You do not need to be woken hourly.
- A responsible adult should remain with you for the first 24 hours.

FOLLOW-UP
- Follow up with your primary care physician in 3 days.
- Follow up with neurology in 2 weeks if symptoms persist.

RETURN TO THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT IMMEDIATELY FOR:
- A headache that is severe or progressively worsening
- Repeated emesis
- Seizure activity
- Confusion, disorientation, or difficulty rousing
- Unequal pupils, diplopia, or slurred speech
- New weakness or numbness
- Clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - ACUTE PYELONEPHRITIS

Diagnosis: acute pyelonephritis, left kidney. Urine culture grew E. coli sensitive to ciprofloxacin.

Medications
- Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 10 days. Complete the full course even once you feel well.
- Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN fever or flank pain.
- Ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN nausea.

Precautions while taking ciprofloxacin
- Do not take antacids, calcium, or iron within 2 hours of a dose. They impair absorption.
- Avoid prolonged sun exposure. This antibiotic causes photosensitivity.
- Report any tendon pain immediately and discontinue the drug.

Supportive care
- Increase oral fluid intake to at least 2 litres daily.
- Void frequently and completely.

Activity
- No strenuous exercise for 1 week.
- You may return to work in 3 days if afebrile.

Follow-up
- Follow up with your primary care physician in 4 days.
- Repeat urine culture in 2 weeks.
- A renal ultrasound has been ordered; the imaging department will call you.

Return to the emergency department for temperature above 101 F after 48 hours of antibiotics, intractable vomiting preventing oral intake, worsening flank pain, hypotension or near-syncope, or decreased urine output.

TOTAL KNEE ARTHROPLASTY: DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS

MEDICATIONS
- Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous QD for 14 days for thromboprophylaxis.
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg PO q8h scheduled, not PRN.
- Oxycodone 5 mg PO q4h PRN pain. Maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours.
- Ondansetron 4 mg sublingual q8h PRN nausea.
- Senna 8.6 mg PO BID.

WOUND CARE
- The dressing is waterproof. Showers are permitted. Do not submerge the knee.
- Do not apply any ointment or cream to the incision.

ACTIVITY AND WEIGHT-BEARING
- Weight-bearing as tolerated with the walker.
- Perform the prescribed range of motion exercises 3 times a day.
- Elevate the extremity when seated.
- Apply ice for 20 minutes every 2 hours while awake.
- Do not drive for 6 weeks or while taking oxycodone.
- No stairs unassisted for 2 weeks.

FOLLOW-UP
- Physical therapy begins in 2 days and continues 3 times weekly.
- Follow up with orthopedics in 3 weeks.

Contact the orthopedic service immediately if you develop calf pain, unilateral lower extremity edema, fever above 101 F, wound dehiscence, purulent drainage, or erythema spreading from the incision. Call 911 for acute dyspnea or chest pain, which may indicate pulmonary embolism.
